title: Prayer
definition: Prayer is the believer’s communion with God through praise, confession, thanksgiving, intercession, dependence, and request in the name of Jesus.
summary: Prayer is the believer’s communion with God through praise, confession, thanksgiving, intercession, dependence, and request in the name of Jesus.
christFocus: Jesus teaches His people to pray, brings them near to the Father, and gives the Holy Spirit to help them in weakness.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Prayer is not performance before God. It is the child of God coming to the Father through Christ with honesty, reverence, need, worship, and trust.

Scripture shows many kinds of prayer: praise, lament, confession, thanksgiving, intercession, and surrender. Believers can pray in joy, weakness, grief, temptation, confusion, and need.

Prayer depends on Christ and the Spirit. Jesus gives access to the Father, and the Holy Spirit helps believers when they do not know how to pray as they should.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Many believers feel they must sound spiritual before they can pray. Prayer invites the weak, ashamed, tired, and struggling to come near because Christ has opened the way.

This doctrine also keeps Christian life from becoming self-powered. Prayer teaches dependence instead of control.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Come to God honestly through Christ. Pray Scripture, confess sin, ask for help, intercede for others, and rely on the Holy Spirit when your words feel weak.
